text:
In TextOS, each part has a hard evidence boundary: the writer may use only the evidence assigned to that part, and nothing else can be brought in there. When a factual part has no usable evidence, the part is refused instead of being filled. A refused part shows exactly where material is missing, while a gap filled with invented text would read like any other sentence.

The writer's answer is then read strictly: its format has to match exactly, unknown fields are refused, each cited evidence reference has to exist in the supplied set, and a malformed or incomplete answer is rejected rather than requested again. That strictness matters because a loosely read answer is where unsupported material tends to slip in.
